2.text: swiftly driven sledge, keeping it from tipping over. After twenty-four hours

3.text: of this painful exercise, the driver is often so tired, that, on reaching the

4.text: place, he reels like one drunk, and has to be helped into the house.

5.text: Of two drivers who took part in the dog-race of 1869, which I mentioned

6.text: before, the victor so impaired his health by the strain that he never recovered.

7.text: The young girls and women among the Chukchee have foot-races of their

8.text: own, which they are as eager to win as the men. Often foot-races are run by

9.text: boys, who compete with fellows of their own age.
9.note: Printed as "who" + U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT + "compete", a raised mid-height dot between the words with no space, not a comma and not a baseline period. Ruled a printer's blot (keying_spec.md §2.14: a printer's error in punctuation is a blot, keyed as nothing, class artifact) and dropped, with a normal interword space keyed instead. Same defect recurs on this page at lines 36 and 37.

10.text: Wrestling usually takes place after the foot-race, because the wrestlers

11.text: strip naked to the waist, and they like to have their bodies heated by the

12.text: previous exercise. If there is no foot-race, the wrestlers will run a couple of

13.text: miles to get warmed up for their contests. While the couples are wrestling,

14.text: the rest of the people sit or stand around to judge the matches. Sometimes

15.text: two or three pairs wrestle at the same time. After stripping, the men, just

16.text: before the contest, rub their bodies all over with snow.

17.text: The rules of the contest require that one man shall assume a posture

18.text: of passive defence, and the other try to throw him. The first is called

19.text: “motionless” (uˊlvɪlɪn); the second, “the attacking one” (viriˊtɪlɪn). If the latter
19.resolved: uˊlvɪlɪn = u + U+02CA + l + v + U+026A + l + U+026A + n; viriˊtɪlɪn = v + i + r + i + U+02CA + t + U+026A + l + U+026A + n
19.note: Both raised marks are the angled stress tick, keyed U+02CA per keying_spec.md §4/§5.8 (raised mark defaults to stress, never apostrophe). Confirmed at 4x: in both words the letters after the stress mark (l,v,ɪ,l,ɪ,n and t,ɪ,l,ɪ,n) are dotless small-cap ɪ (U+026A), shorter and serifed top/bottom, contrasted against the dotted lowercase i's in "viri" on the same word before the mark. Both quote pairs normalized to curly “ ” per §1/§5.6 — the machine draft had the second pair as straight \" ... \".

20.text: proves unsuccessful, the positions are reversed. Finally there usually follows

21.text: a rough-and-tumble scramble, in which each of the contestants tries every

22.text: means to get the better of his adversary. Custom requires that one of the

23.text: parties be made to touch the ground with both of his shoulders, and kept

24.text: in this position in spite of his struggles. Three bouts are regarded as settling

25.text: the match, but the vanquished one often desires to keep on trying his

26.text: chances. Frequently he becomes greatly excited, and then a violent scuffle

27.text: may ensue. The victor has to meet the winner of any other contests: but,

28.text: lest he should become too tired, he will step back after a few matches and

29.text: return in a half-hour or so to try his chance once more. This continues until

30.text: the best man is determined, and he takes the stake if there is one. The

31.text: passions are aroused quite enough, however, without stakes, so that prizes

32.text: are seldom put up for this sport. Several Chukchee tales describe a peculiar

33.text: wrestling-match that takes place on a spread walrus-skin, slippery with blubber

34.text: and made dangerous by having sharp splinters of bone or wood stuck around

35.text: its edge. Similar details are mentioned also in Eskimo and Indian tales.¹
35.note: Footnote reference marker keyed as superscript ¹ (U+00B9) per keying_spec.md §2.10, tight against the period; the machine draft rendered it as a bare "!".

36.text: A wrestling-match is the usual method of settling quarrels among the
36.note: Printed as "usual" + U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT + "method", the same raised mid-dot artifact as line 9 (keying_spec.md §2.14, blot, keyed as nothing).

37.text: Chukchee. A man having a grudge against another one will either openly
37.note: Printed as "A man. having", a small raised dot after "man" with no sentence break in sense; the same blot family as lines 9 and 36 (keying_spec.md §2.14), keyed as nothing.

38.text: challenge him for a match or he will seek a chance to encounter him in a

39.text: general contest. In either case, the match sometimes ends in bloodshed, or

40.text: even death, if the spectators do not interfere in time.

41.text: Women also wrestle, but their matches generally end in scratching and

42.text: pulling hair. Members of alien tribes are also allowed to take part in all of
